# Overview

Short patterns for scripts and code-generating tools that use onedevr. Each
section names the mistake first and shows the working form. Every call here is
checked by the package tests: it only uses arguments that exist. For the list
of functions see `vignette("function-map")`; for complete workflows see
`vignette("issues-workflow")`, `vignette("pull-requests-workflow")` and
`vignette("builds-workflow")`.

```r
library(onedevr)
```

# 1. Connections

onedevr picks the connection in this order: an explicit `conn` argument, then
the default set with `od_set_connection()`, then the `ONEDEV_*` environment
variables (`od_get_config()`).

```r
# Explicit connection: best for scripts that talk to more than one instance
conn <- od_connection(
  host = "https://git.example.test",
  token = Sys.getenv("ONEDEV_API_TOKEN"),
  project_path = "group/my-project"
)
issues <- od_query_issues(state = "Open", conn = conn)

# Printing a connection masks the token and password
conn
```

**Pitfall:** `od_set_connection()` sets a package-wide default. A call that
forgets `conn =` then silently uses it, possibly against the wrong host.

```r
# Safer: set a default once, pass conn explicitly for the exceptions
od_set_connection(conn)
staging <- od_connection(
  host = "https://staging.example.test",
  token = Sys.getenv("ONEDEV_API_TOKEN"),
  project_path = "group/my-project"
)
od_query_issues(state = "Open", conn = staging)
```

**Who am I?** `od_whoami()` returns the login name, for example for an
`Assignee` field. When the server refuses `GET /users/me` (HTTP 401/403/404), it
falls back to the connection's username. Set `ONEDEV_USERNAME` together with
`ONEDEV_AUTH=bearer` to provide the name and keep token authentication.

```r
od_create_issue("Check the build", fields = list(Assignee = od_whoami()))
```

# 2. UI numbers, not internal ids

The number you see in the web UI (`#145`) is not the REST `id`. Every high-level
function takes the UI number and resolves the id itself.

```r
od_get_issue(145)
od_get_issue("#145")          # the same
od_get_pull_request(42)
od_get_build(100)

# Only for debugging: pass an internal id explicitly
od_get_issue(283, use_internal_id = TRUE)
```

# 3. Project scope

Most functions use the project of the connection (`project_path`) or of the
environment (`ONEDEV_PROJECT_PATH`). They have no `project` argument.

```r
# One call against another project: use a connection for it
other <- od_connection(
  host = "https://git.example.test",
  token = Sys.getenv("ONEDEV_API_TOKEN"),
  project_path = "other/project"
)
od_query_issues(state = "Open", conn = other)

# A few functions take a `project` argument directly
od_list_iterations(project = "other/project")
od_query_commits(count = 20L, project = "other/project")
```

# 4. Queries

OneDev has its own query language, not SQL. Print the grammar of your instance
instead of guessing:

```r
cat(od_get_query_description("issue"))
```

Rules that avoid most HTTP 406 "Invalid query" errors:

- Field names are quoted: `"State" is "Open"`.
- Field names differ per instance. A field such as `IsResolved` may not exist;
  use the state instead (`state = "Closed"`).
- For text search use fuzzy text `~text~`. `"Title" contains "..."` is often
  rejected.
- State names must match the board exactly (`"In Progress"`, `"Closed"`).

```r
od_query_issues(query = "~GeoJSON~")
od_query_issues(query = '"Iteration" is "Version 3.0.0"', state = "Open")
```

Values you pass as `state` (and as `iteration` to `od_query_board_issues()`)
are quoted and escaped for you. In a raw `query` string you must escape quotes
yourself:

```r
quote_value <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\", "\\\\", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub('"', '\\"', x, fixed = TRUE)
  paste0('"', x, '"')
}
od_query_issues(query = paste0('"Assignee" is ', quote_value(od_whoami())))
```

## Large result sets

OneDev returns at most 100 records per request. The list helpers page
automatically when `count` is larger, so a large `count` works:

```r
od_query_issues(state = "Open", count = 450L)
```

To process results page by page, or to cap the work, use `od_paginate()`:

```r
all_open <- od_paginate(od_query_issues, state = "Open", page_size = 100L)
first_pages <- od_paginate(od_query_issues, state = "Open", max_pages = 2L)
```

Filter on the server (in `query`) instead of fetching everything and filtering
in R.

# 5. Return shapes

List helpers return tibbles. Single objects and write helpers return lists.

```r
issues <- od_query_issues(state = "Open")            # tibble
nrow(issues)

raw <- od_query_issues(state = "Open", as_tibble = FALSE)   # list of records
vapply(raw, function(x) x$title, character(1))

# Switch the default for a session
options(onedevr.as_tibble = FALSE)
```

An empty result is a tibble with 0 rows, not an error. Check before indexing:

```r
open <- od_query_issues(state = "Open")
if (nrow(open) > 0) {
  first <- open[1, ]
}
```

# 6. Errors

HTTP errors are conditions of class `od_http_error` with the fields `status`,
`method` and `url`. Branch on the status instead of parsing the message:

```r
result <- tryCatch(
  od_get_issue(999999),
  od_http_error = function(e) {
    if (e$status == 404) NULL else stop(e)
  }
)
```

Things worth knowing:

- Error messages that contain an HTML page (for example HTTP 500 "Interner
  Fehler") are shortened to the page title.
- Some write endpoints accept more than one body shape. onedevr tries the known
  ones and reports every failure together, so the real cause is visible.
- **Comments:** `POST /issue-comments` has returned HTTP 500 on some instances.
  Before retrying, check whether the comment was created anyway, to avoid
  duplicates:

```r
tryCatch(
  od_add_issue_comment(145, "Merged to main"),
  od_http_error = function(e) {
    if (e$status == 500) {
      comments <- od_get_issue_comments(145, as_tibble = FALSE)
      message("Server error; the issue now has ", length(comments), " comments")
    }
    stop(e)
  }
)
```

# 7. Escape hatch

When no helper exists, `od_request()` reaches any endpoint with the same
connection and error handling. The endpoint list of your instance is at
`https://<host>/~help/api`.

```r
od_request("GET", "/projects", query = list(count = 5L))
od_request("POST", "/issues/283/title", body = "New title")
```

# 8. Experimental areas

Batch, parallel, streaming, caching, webhook and SSH-key functions are marked
**Experimental** in their help pages: they are tested offline only and their
interface may change. Prefer the core functions above in automation until they
are verified.
